editor_note: The permission tables are rendered faithfully in consistent informal "tú" ("Revisa", "Listar tus backends"), with job→trabajo, backend kept as backend and "Close job session"→"Cerrar la sesión del trabajo", and no drift in any endpoint description.

The translation is faithful and natural: "skills" is rendered consistently as "habilidades" in "Registro de cambios de las habilidades de Qiskit", and "Se lanzó la habilidad ... para migrar código de qiskit-ibm-runtime" keeps the source's meaning exactly.

The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. Terms are correct and consistent: "primitiva Executor", "mitigación y supresión de errores", "cancelación probabilística de errores (PEC)", "postselección basada en mediciones", and the beta caveat plus the "0.47.0 o posterior" version requirement are both kept. Two small polish points: entry [16] says "notas de la versión de todas las versiones", which repeats itself awkwardly. Entry [5] turns "first previewed" into "presentadas por primera vez", which loses the sense that QDC 2025 only showed a preview.

examples.source: To see the release notes for all versions, visit the ...
examples.translation: Para ver las notas de la versión de todas las versiones, visita las ...
examples.suggested: Para consultar las notas de todas las versiones, visita las ...
examples.why: The phrase "versión ... versiones" repeats itself and reads like a word-for-word calque.

examples.source: both of which were first previewed at QDC 2025
examples.translation: ambas presentadas por primera vez en QDC 2025
examples.suggested: ambas mostradas en versión preliminar en QDC 2025
examples.why: "Previewed" means an early look, not a full presentation. This is a slight shift in nuance but does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. Every caveat and condition carries over correctly: the 10 minutes per 28-day rolling window, not entering credit card details unless you are upgrading, the 32-digit code, and the account ID step without which the account is not activated. The problems are small wording slips. IBM's plan name "Open Plan" is translated as "Plan Abierto", which learners won't find in the IBM Quantum interface. The admonition in [7] uses the passive calque "Si eres aprobado". In [29] the grammatical number shifts: "El usuario recibirá" and "podrá" are singular, but "No necesitarán" is plural.

examples.source: under the Open Plan ... The Open Plan provides 10 minutes
examples.translation: bajo el Plan Abierto ... El Plan Abierto proporciona 10 minutos
examples.suggested: con el plan Open Plan ... El Open Plan proporciona 10 minutos
examples.why: Open Plan is IBM's product/plan name as it appears in the Platform UI; translating it makes it harder for learners to match the docs to what they see on screen.

examples.source: If you are approved for a Classroom Account
examples.translation: Si eres aprobado para una cuenta de aula
examples.suggested: Si te aprueban la cuenta de aula
examples.why: Passive 'ser aprobado para' is a calque of the English; the active impersonal reads more natural in Spanish.

examples.source: The user will receive an invitation ... They will not need to enter credit card information
examples.translation: El usuario recibirá una invitación ... No necesitarán introducir información de tarjeta de crédito
examples.suggested: El usuario recibirá una invitación ... No necesitará introducir información de tarjeta de crédito
examples.why: English singular 'they' was carried over as a plural verb, so it no longer agrees with the singular subject 'El usuario' (the next line correctly uses 'podrá').

editor_note: Rewritten entry 4 is faithful and natural: "Te recomendamos usar estas versiones o más recientes" keeps the "or newer" qualifier and the informal tú register.

All three rewritten entries are faithful and natural. Entries 25 and 40 use "Documentación de la API de `environment`/`execution`". Entry 40 translates init_qubits correctly as "restablecer los qubits al estado fundamental para cada shot". Entry 51 uses the informal "Revisa la documentación de la API [ExecutionOptionsV2]".

All four rewritten entries (4, 5, 6, 27) say the same thing as the English. Nothing would mislead a learner: the technique list, the v0.50.0 client-side/Executor claim, the "largely drop-in" hedge and every link target are intact. Two phrasing slips remain. In entry 6, "con el único cambio siendo la declaración de importación" copies the English gerund construction, which is not idiomatic Spanish. In entry 5, "pre y post procesamiento" should be "preprocesamiento y posprocesamiento".

examples.source: with the only change being the import statement
examples.translation: con el único cambio siendo la declaración de importación
examples.suggested: y el único cambio necesario es la sentencia de importación
examples.why: This copies the English gerund construction, which is not idiomatic Spanish. A native writer would use a finite clause here.

examples.source: perform most of the pre- and post-processing on the client side
examples.translation: realizan la mayor parte del pre y post procesamiento en el lado del cliente
examples.suggested: realizan la mayor parte del preprocesamiento y el posprocesamiento del lado del cliente
examples.why: Spanish writes these prefixes attached to the word, so 'pre y post procesamiento' is wrong. The standard terms are 'preprocesamiento' and 'posprocesamiento'. 'del lado del cliente' also reads more naturally than 'en el lado del cliente'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The HA/DR definitions, the three-zone setup with no single point of failure, and the claim of no noticeable degradation during a zonal failure all match the English. There are two small editorial problems. The product name is translated as "Servicio de Cómputo Cuántico de IBM" in [0], but [4] keeps the brand name "IBM Quantum Compute Service", so the page names the service two ways. Also, "multi-zona" in [8] should be written as one word, "multizona", following RAE rules for prefixes.

examples.source: IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.translation: Servicio de Cómputo Cuántico de IBM
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Compute Service
examples.why: [4] keeps the product name in English, so the page is inconsistent. Brand names are usually left untranslated.

examples.source: a multi-zone region
examples.translation: una región multi-zona
examples.suggested: una región multizona
examples.why: RAE rules say prefixes like multi- attach directly to the word, without a hyphen.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and nothing in it would mislead a learner. Terms are correct and used the same way throughout: "notas de versión", "política de obsolescencia", "paquete cliente", and informal "tú" forms such as "Instala" and "sigue". There is one small problem in the "Recomendaciones" list in entry [11]. The English items are all imperatives, but the Spanish opens with the infinitive "Instalar el SDK de Qiskit desde el código fuente" and then switches to the imperatives "Ejecuta", "Prueba" and "Revisa". A native editor would make the first item "Instala" so the list is parallel.

examples.source: [Install the Qiskit SDK from source](/guides/install-qiskit-source).
examples.translation: [Instalar el SDK de Qiskit desde el código fuente](/guides/install-qiskit-source).
examples.suggested: [Instala el SDK de Qiskit desde el código fuente](/guides/install-qiskit-source).
examples.why: This item uses the infinitive, but the other items in the same list use the tú imperative (Ejecuta, Prueba, Revisa). The English uses imperatives throughout, so the list should match.

editor_note: Entry 9 is faithful and reads naturally: the translation keeps the conditional "si habilitas el Pauli-twirling en tu trabajo de Sampler" and the claim that the total "shots se basa en" `num_randomizations` and `shots_per_randomization`, and it uses the same informal register and the same "trabajo"/"shots" terms as entries 7-8.

The 43 rewritten entries keep the English meaning, and the key conditions come through intact, including "solo funciona con el Estimator heredado del lado del servidor" (entry 10) and "solo acepta modelos de ruido para capas de dos qubits aprendidos con el protocolo Pauli-Lindblad" (entry 38); the informal tú register holds throughout ("planees", "Reutiliza", "Ten en cuenta").

All five rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 8 keeps both "solo funciona con" restrictions and the v0.50.0 caveat. Entry 17 keeps the option list. The one problem is in entry 36: "helper program" is rendered as "programa ayudante", but the rest of the page uses "programa asistente" (entries 11 and 25, plus "asistente de aprendizaje de ruido" in entries 0 and 1). Entry 36 should use "programa asistente" to match. Entries 35 and 38 need no changes.

examples.source: The following code shows how to use the helper program with the new client-side Estimator
examples.translation: El siguiente código muestra cómo usar el programa ayudante con el nuevo Estimator del lado del cliente
examples.suggested: El siguiente código muestra cómo usar el programa asistente con el nuevo Estimator del lado del cliente
examples.why: Elsewhere on the page, 'helper program' is consistently 'programa asistente' (entries 11, 25). 'Ayudante' breaks that consistency and reads less idiomatically in technical Spanish.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries (12, 28, 42) would mislead a learner. All numbers, node counts, the Hamming-weight-1 hard-constraint caveat and the table figures match the English. There are two small wording issues. In entry 28, "Modelo de espín-vidrio de Ising" copies the English word order for "spin glass"; the usual Spanish term is "vidrio de espín", so it should read "Modelo de vidrio de espín de Ising". In entry 12, "con restricciones aplicadas como restricciones estrictas" repeats "restricciones" and reads stiffly. Entry 42 reads naturally ("subdiccionario ... que ayuda a verificar el orden").

examples.source: Ising spin-glass model
examples.translation: Modelo de espín-vidrio de Ising
examples.suggested: Modelo de vidrio de espín de Ising
examples.why: The usual Spanish term for spin glass is "vidrio de espín". "espín-vidrio" copies the English word order. The meaning is still recognizable, so this is minor.

examples.source: with constraints enforced as hard Hamming-weight-1 constraints rather than penalty terms
examples.translation: con restricciones aplicadas como restricciones estrictas de peso de Hamming 1 en lugar de términos de penalización
examples.suggested: y las restricciones se imponen como restricciones estrictas de peso de Hamming 1, no como términos de penalización
examples.why: Saying "restricciones" twice makes the sentence stiff and hard to follow. Turning it into its own clause with "se imponen" reads more naturally, and the meaning stays the same.

editor_note: Faithful and natural in informal tú ("Consulta las siguientes guías", "Instala el nuevo paquete"), and "does break compatibility" is kept at full strength as "rompe la compatibilidad con todas las versiones anteriores".

The five rewritten entries (7, 20, 21, 33, 34) are faithful and natural: entry 7 keeps the negation ("los usuarios de tu cuenta no pueden verse entre sí, aunque tengan acceso a los mismos recursos"), entry 21 keeps "el conjunto mínimo de permisos", and entries 33/34 keep the region labels as "Servicio de Cómputo de IBM Quantum - región us-east/eu-de" with the host lists unchanged.

Entry 6 is faithful and reads naturally. "normalmente se inserta un reset implícito al comienzo del circuito" keeps the "typically" hedge, "reset" matches its use in entry 7, and `init_qubits` is correctly called an "indicador" set as an "opción de ejecución de primitivas".

None of the five rewritten entries (6, 11, 12, 30, 37) changes the meaning. The overlap caveat in [37] and the optional-shots and bind-only-if-Parameter conditions in [11] are intact. Three things are worth fixing. First, QPU switches gender: [30] says "en la QPU" but [37] says "un QPU", and the rest of the page ([14]) uses the masculine. Second, [37] has calques: "La garantía que se hace" and "definitivamente ocurrieron" read as translationese. Third, "bind" appears as both "se asignan al circuito" and "deben vincularse" in the same list item of [11]. This is defensible but slightly inconsistent.

examples.source: when particular shots were executed on the QPU
examples.translation: cuándo se ejecutaron determinados shots en la QPU
examples.suggested: cuándo se ejecutaron determinados shots en el QPU
examples.why: QPU is feminine here but masculine in [37] ("un QPU") and [14] ("a un QPU"). One gender should be used across the file.

examples.source: The guarantee being made is that the referenced data definitely occurred in the reported execution span
examples.translation: La garantía que se hace es que los datos referenciados definitivamente ocurrieron en el span de ejecución reportado
examples.suggested: Lo que se garantiza es que los datos referenciados se obtuvieron con certeza dentro del span de ejecución indicado
examples.why: "La garantía que se hace" and "definitivamente" are calques of the English. A native technical writer would say "Lo que se garantiza" and "con certeza".

examples.source: A collection of parameter values to bind the circuit against $\theta_k$ (only needed if any `Parameter` objects are used that must be bound at runtime)
examples.translation: Una colección de valores de parámetros $\theta_k$ que se asignan al circuito (solo es necesario si se utilizan objetos `Parameter` que deben vincularse en tiempo de ejecución)
examples.suggested: Una colección de valores de parámetros $\theta_k$ que se vinculan al circuito (solo es necesario si se utilizan objetos `Parameter` que deben vincularse en tiempo de ejecución)
examples.why: The same verb "bind" is rendered two ways in one bullet (asignan / vincularse). A single verb makes it clearer that both halves refer to the same operation.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning and read naturally. Entry 7 renders "badging exam" as "el examen para obtener la insignia de «Fundamentos de la información cuántica»", and entry 12 uses the standard GDPR term "encargado del tratamiento de datos externo" for "third-party data processor" and keeps every caveat (US location, data shared with subsidiaries and third parties).

Entry 29 (the Credly privacy notice) keeps the meaning of the English: the data shared (name, email, badge), Credly's role as an authorized data processor in the US, the "may share" with subsidiaries and third parties, and both links all match. Two English calques remain that a native legal or technical editor would fix. "Se manejará de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad" uses the false friend "consistente con" where Spanish would say "de conformidad con". "propósitos operacionales" would normally be "fines operativos", and the passive "será compartida con Credly" reads more naturally as "se compartirá con Credly".

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Se manejará de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.suggested: Se tratará de conformidad con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.why: 'consistente con' is a false-friend calque of 'consistent with'. In legal and privacy Spanish the usual phrase is 'de conformidad con' or 'conforme a'.

examples.source: for program reporting and operational purposes
examples.translation: para informes del programa y propósitos operacionales
examples.suggested: con fines de elaboración de informes del programa y fines operativos
examples.why: 'propósitos operacionales' copies the English wording. Spanish privacy notices say 'fines operativos'. The meaning is unchanged, so this is a minor issue.

editor_note: In entry [6], "viewed collectively as single systems" is translated as "pueden verse colectivamente como sistemas individuales". In Spanish that reads as "separate, individual systems", which is the opposite of the lesson's key idea that several systems can be treated as ONE compound system. The very next sentence then uses "sistemas individuales" for the individual subsystems being measured, so the same phrase ends up meaning two opposite things. Two smaller points: [6] adds "especialmente" before "al analizar algoritmos", which slightly shifts the emphasis, and [2] uses the calque "Alternativamente". The rest is faithful, including "entrelazamiento", "único sistema compuesto" in [5] and the tú register.

examples.source: than simply recognizing that they may be viewed collectively as single systems.
examples.translation: que simplemente reconocer que pueden verse colectivamente como sistemas individuales.
examples.suggested: que simplemente reconocer que pueden verse colectivamente como un único sistema.
examples.why: 'sistemas individuales' means separate, individual systems, which inverts the idea that the systems together form one compound system. It also clashes with the next sentence, where 'sistemas individuales' correctly means the individual subsystems.

examples.source: and it is important to understand exactly how when analyzing quantum algorithms and protocols.
examples.translation: y es importante comprender exactamente cómo — especialmente al analizar algoritmos y protocolos cuánticos.
examples.suggested: y es importante comprender exactamente cómo lo hace al analizar algoritmos y protocolos cuánticos.
examples.why: 'especialmente' is not in the source. The added word turns 'when analyzing' into a general claim with extra emphasis. The shift is small, so this is minor.

examples.source: Alternatively, you can open the YouTube video
examples.translation: Alternativamente, puedes abrir el video de YouTube
examples.suggested: También puedes abrir el video de YouTube
examples.why: 'Alternativamente' at the start of a sentence is a calque from English. 'También puedes' reads more naturally in Spanish.

editor_note: Entry 61 keeps the meaning (the code does not protect Q), so it would not mislead a learner. Two things still need fixing. First, "falla en proteger" is a calque of "fails to protect"; natural Spanish would be "no logra proteger" or "no protege". Second, entry 59 already reads "De lo contrario, el código falla con probabilidad", so the page renders "el código falla con probabilidad [fórmula] el código falla en proteger a Q". That repeats "el código falla" and breaks the sentence. The fix is either to restore 59 to "De lo contrario, con probabilidad" or to make 61 continue 59 as it stands.

examples.source: the code fails to protect $\mathsf{Q}$.
examples.translation: el código falla en proteger a $\mathsf{Q}$.
examples.suggested: el código no logra proteger a $\mathsf{Q}$. (with entry 59 as "De lo contrario, con probabilidad")
examples.why: "Fallar en + infinitivo" is an anglicism for "fail to". Also, entry 59 already says "el código falla con probabilidad", so the rendered sentence says "el código falla" twice around the formula.

editor_note: Entries 3 and 7 keep the meaning of the English, including the stressed negation "*no* depende del tamaño del circuito cuántico" and "cierto umbral finito". Entry 4 has two phrasing slips a native editor would fix. "nunca quedan desprotegidos por un código corrector" is awkward, and the "por" could be read as "left unprotected by a code". It should say "nunca quedan sin la protección de un código…". "deben ser implementadas" is a calque of the English passive, and "deben implementarse" reads more naturally. Neither slip would mislead a learner.

examples.source: logical qubits that never go without the protection of a quantum error correcting code
examples.translation: qubits *lógicos* que nunca quedan desprotegidos por un código corrector de errores cuánticos
examples.suggested: qubits *lógicos* que nunca quedan sin la protección de un código corrector de errores cuánticos
examples.why: 'desprotegidos por' is awkward and can read as if the code is what leaves the qubits unprotected. 'sin la protección de' matches the English and reads naturally.

examples.source: the actual computations we're interested in performing must be implemented
examples.translation: las computaciones reales que deseamos realizar deben ser implementadas
examples.suggested: las computaciones que realmente nos interesa realizar deben implementarse
examples.why: The 'ser + participio' passive copies the English structure. The reflexive passive is the idiomatic choice in Spanish technical prose.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. "modelo de consulta", "placa de Petri", "ventajas medibles" and "algoritmo de Deutsch-Jozsa" are all correct, and the tú register holds ("puedes abrir"). There are two small naturalness issues. Entry [5] renders "discuss" twice as "discutimos", which is a calque: in Spanish "discutir" leans toward "argue" or "debate", and "analizamos/estudiamos" reads more natively. Entry [7] uses "Alternativamente", an English-style adverb where "También puedes abrir…" is more idiomatic.

examples.source: we'll discuss the very first quantum algorithm that was discovered
examples.translation: discutimos el primer algoritmo cuántico jamás descubierto
examples.suggested: analizamos el primer algoritmo cuántico jamás descubierto
examples.why: 'Discutir' is a calque of 'discuss' and suggests debate. 'Analizar/estudiar' is the natural choice in teaching prose. The same issue occurs again later in the entry ('A continuación, discutimos…').

examples.source: Alternatively, you can open the YouTube video
examples.translation: Alternativamente, puedes abrir el video de YouTube
examples.suggested: También puedes abrir el video de YouTube
examples.why: 'Alternativamente' as a sentence opener is translationese. A native writer would use 'También' or 'Si lo prefieres'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally. It uses the informal tú throughout ("realiza el examen", "tu insignia"), and the core terms are right: matrices de densidad, canales, mediciones generales. Two small drifts would still be worth fixing. In [10], "gain knowledge on" becomes "adquirir una comprensión sólida", which adds a promise of solid understanding that the English does not make. In [17], "third-party data processor" is shortened to "proveedor externo" and "to assist in the administration" to "para administrar", which loses the data-processor role in this privacy notice. Neither would mislead a learner about quantum information.

examples.source: who are eager to gain knowledge on the theoretical foundations
examples.translation: que deseen adquirir una comprensión sólida de los fundamentos teóricos
examples.suggested: que deseen adquirir conocimientos sobre los fundamentos teóricos
examples.why: 'sólida' is not in the English. It makes the course sound like it promises more than it does.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM ... to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: un proveedor externo autorizado por IBM con sede en los Estados Unidos, para administrar el programa
examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM, con sede en los Estados Unidos, para ayudar a administrar el programa
examples.why: This drops the 'data processor' role, which carries legal meaning in a privacy notice. 'para administrar' also makes Credly sound like it runs the program when the English says it only helps administer it.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (28, 31, 62) keep the English meaning. The 10,000-city example, "orders of magnitude longer than the age of our Sun", the exponential-growth claim and the caveats about RAM, measurement, node co-location and scheduling all come through intact. Entry 62 translates "scheduling control" as "control de programación". In Spanish, "programación" usually reads as "programming", and entry 42 already uses "planificación de recursos" for scheduling, so it should be "control de planificación". Entry 31's "cada computador jamás construido" copies the English "every computer ever built" word for word. A native writer would say "todos los computadores construidos hasta hoy". Entry 28 is fine.

examples.source: users of quantum resources will often not have the same level of scheduling control
examples.translation: no tendrán el mismo nivel de control de programación
examples.suggested: no tendrán el mismo nivel de control sobre la planificación (de trabajos)
examples.why: In an HPC context, 'programación' reads as 'programming', not job scheduling. Entry 42 of the same file translates scheduling as 'planificación', so this is also an inconsistency within the file.

examples.source: even if every computer ever built tested one route per microsecond
examples.translation: incluso si cada computador jamás construido probara una ruta por microsegundo
examples.suggested: incluso si todos los computadores construidos hasta hoy probaran una ruta por microsegundo
examples.why: 'cada ... jamás construido' copies the English phrasing word for word and reads stiffly. The meaning is correct.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The course overview, the exam instructions and the Credly privacy notice all say what the English says, and the informal tú register holds ("Aprenderás", "Completa el curso", "realiza el examen"). The only problems are two anglicisms in the Credly notice [11]. "de manera consistente con" is a calque of "consistent with", and "conforme a" or "de acuerdo con" is the natural Spanish. "subsidiarias de IBM" would normally be "filiales de IBM" in Spanish corporate and legal text.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Se tratarán de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.suggested: Se tratarán conforme a las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.why: "De manera consistente con" copies the English "consistent with"; Spanish legal text uses "conforme a" or "de acuerdo con".

examples.source: IBM may share the personal information collected with IBM subsidiaries and third parties globally.
examples.translation: IBM puede compartir los datos personales recopilados con subsidiarias de IBM y terceros en todo el mundo.
examples.suggested: IBM puede compartir los datos personales recopilados con filiales de IBM y terceros en todo el mundo.
examples.why: "Filiales" is the usual Spanish word for corporate subsidiaries; "subsidiarias" is an anglicism, although it is common in Latin America.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and the informal tú register is used consistently ("puedes avanzar a tu propio ritmo", "Te recomendamos"). In [8] and [9], "badge" is left in English. Spanish IBM material and Spanish technical writing normally say "insignia", and "Obtención del badge" reads as a calque. [9] also renders "badging exam" as "examen de certificación". That slightly overstates what a digital badge is, although it would not really mislead a learner. [5] "navegar este curso" is missing the usual preposition ("navegar por este curso").

examples.source: Earning the Quantum Business Foundations badge
examples.translation: Obtención del badge Quantum Business Foundations
examples.suggested: Cómo obtener la insignia Quantum Business Foundations
examples.why: 'badge' is an unnecessary anglicism; IBM's Spanish materials use 'insignia'. The nominal 'Obtención del...' also reads stiffly.

examples.source: take a badging exam if you wish. Upon passing the badging exam you will earn your IBM Quantum Business Foundations badge.
examples.translation: realizar un examen de certificación si lo deseas. Al aprobar el examen, obtendrás tu badge IBM Quantum Business Foundations.
examples.suggested: realizar el examen para obtener la insignia si lo deseas. Al aprobarlo, obtendrás tu insignia IBM Quantum Business Foundations.
examples.why: 'examen de certificación' slightly overstates a badging exam, and 'badge' should be 'insignia', as in entry 8.

examples.source: Tips for navigating this course
examples.translation: Consejos para navegar este curso
examples.suggested: Consejos para navegar por este curso
examples.why: In Spanish, 'navegar' is normally followed by 'por' when it means moving through content.

editor_note: Entry 21, the rewritten Credly privacy notice, keeps the meaning of the English. The data shared (name, email address, badge earned), the global sharing with subsidiaries and third parties, the "puede" (may) hedge and both links are all intact, so nothing here would mislead a reader. Two English calques remain that a native legal or technical editor would change. "de manera consistente con" uses "consistente" as a false friend; "de conformidad con" or "conforme a" is the idiomatic choice. "procesador de datos de terceros" is a literal rendering, where Spanish privacy notices say "encargado del tratamiento de datos".

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Serán tratados de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.suggested: Se tratarán de conformidad con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.why: 'Consistente con' copies the English 'consistent with' (a false friend). A native legal text would say 'de conformidad con' or 'conforme a'.

examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un procesador de datos de terceros autorizado por IBM
examples.suggested: un encargado del tratamiento de datos externo autorizado por IBM
examples.why: 'Data processor' is a legal role. Its standard Spanish name in privacy notices (the GDPR / RGPD term) is 'encargado del tratamiento'. 'Procesador de datos de terceros' is a literal rendering and can also be read as 'a processor of third parties' data'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere and nothing would mislead a learner. The overview, prerequisites and exam entries read naturally in the informal tú register ("Explora", "Configura tu entorno", "Si apruebas el examen"). A native editor would still fix two small things in the Credly notice [16]: "de manera consistente con" is a calque of "consistent with" (use "conforme a"), and "subsidiarias" is an anglicism in this context (use "filiales"). As a lesser point, the course name in [11] uses English title case ("Algoritmos de Diagonalización Cuántica"), which Spanish does not.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Se tratarán de manera consistente con las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.suggested: Se tratarán conforme a las prácticas de privacidad de IBM.
examples.why: "De manera consistente con" is a calque of "consistent with". Standard Spanish legal and technical prose uses "conforme a" or "de acuerdo con".

examples.source: IBM may share the personal information collected with IBM subsidiaries and third parties globally.
examples.translation: IBM puede compartir los datos personales recopilados a nivel mundial con subsidiarias de IBM y terceros.
examples.suggested: IBM puede compartir los datos personales recopilados con filiales de IBM y con terceros de todo el mundo.
examples.why: "Subsidiarias" is an anglicism here, and "filiales" is the usual term. Placing "a nivel mundial" right after "recopilados" also makes it read as if the data was collected worldwide.

examples.source: To earn your badge for Quantum diagonalization algorithms
examples.translation: Para obtener tu insignia de Algoritmos de Diagonalización Cuántica
examples.suggested: Para obtener tu insignia de Algoritmos de diagonalización cuántica
examples.why: Spanish capitalizes only the first word of a title. The English source itself uses sentence case here.

editor_note: All four rewritten entries (53, 59, 111, 226) keep their meaning: the O(n^3) comparison, the emphasis in "__no__ ... $\it{alguna}$ base ortonormal", the three recap bullets and the conditions for when KQD is useful all come through unchanged, so nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are consistency only. Entry 111 says "la computadora cuántica" but entry 226 says "los computadores cuánticos", and the rest of the page mixes the two as well (entry 9 "computador", entry 12 "computadora"). Entry 226 also capitalizes "Hamiltonianos", but entry 76 writes "hamiltoniano" in lowercase, which is the normal Spanish form.

examples.source: when quantum computers reach fault-tolerance
examples.translation: cuando los computadores cuánticos alcancen la tolerancia a fallos
examples.suggested: cuando las computadoras cuánticas alcancen la tolerancia a fallos
examples.why: Entry 111, rewritten at the same time, uses "la computadora cuántica". The page should use one form throughout.

examples.source: if the Hamiltonians have too many non-commuting terms
examples.translation: si los Hamiltonianos tienen demasiados términos no conmutantes
examples.suggested: si los hamiltonianos tienen demasiados términos no conmutantes
examples.why: In Spanish this word is written in lowercase, and entry 76 already writes "hamiltoniano". The capital H copies the English.

examples.source: This is finally where quantum computer comes into the picture.
examples.translation: Finalmente, aquí es donde entra en escena la computadora cuántica.
examples.suggested: Finalmente, aquí es donde entra en escena la computadora cuántica. (keep, and use computadora in entry 226 too)
examples.why: The translation is correct. It is listed only as the other half of the computadora/computador split, to show which form to standardize on.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries (8, 39, 72, 84) changes the meaning, and none would mislead a learner. There are three wording slips. In entry 8, "características de datos complejas" can read as "complicated features", when the source means complex-valued features. In entry 72, "rotación en el eje Y" should be "rotación alrededor del eje Y". In entry 84, "Alguna literatura" is a calque of "Some literature". The ordinal superscripts in entry 72 (k^ma, j^mo) follow the page's own convention from entry 18 (1^ra, 4^to), so I left them alone.

examples.source: This could be extended to complex data features.
examples.translation: Esto podría extenderse a características de datos complejas.
examples.suggested: Esto podría extenderse a características de datos con valores complejos.
examples.why: In Spanish, 'complejas' next to 'características' reads more naturally as 'complicated'. 'Con valores complejos' makes clear the source means complex numbers.

examples.source: angle encoding imparts a Y-axis rotation proportional to the data value
examples.translation: la codificación por ángulo produce una rotación en el eje Y proporcional al valor del dato
examples.suggested: la codificación por ángulo aplica una rotación alrededor del eje Y proporcional al valor del dato
examples.why: The standard Spanish phrasing is a rotation 'alrededor del' axis, not 'en el' axis.

examples.source: Some literature might define the encoding such that...
examples.translation: Alguna literatura podría definir la codificación de manera que...
examples.suggested: En algunos textos se define la codificación de modo que...
examples.why: 'Alguna literatura' is a calque of the English. A native technical writer would say 'algunos textos' or 'parte de la bibliografía'.

editor_note: Entry 51 is faithful and natural: "Porque los dispositivos reales tienen ruido. Las puertas y las mediciones no son perfectas" keeps the noise explanation and the "occasional errors" hedge, and the concessive "aunque el simulador no los mostró" correctly says the simulator did not show 01/10.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. In [20], "Cuantas más ejecuciones (o *shots*) realice, más precisos serán los resultados" keeps the accuracy-versus-cost trade-off intact, and "shots" matches entry [21]. In [27], "cuya eigenbasis sí conocemos" keeps the contrast in "we do know", and "eigenbasis" (feminine) is used the same way as in entry [44].

None of the three rewritten entries changes the meaning, and entry 140 ("Iniciar en $i=0$ si tenemos un problema similar...") is faithful and natural. Entry 41, "Búsqueda de subespacio VQE (SSVQE)", copies the English word order: "VQE" is left hanging after the noun phrase, so the heading reads as "search of subspace VQE" rather than "a VQE that searches subspaces". Entry 11, "Eigensolver Cuántico Variacional", uses English-style Title Case, while the sibling headings in this file use Spanish sentence case ("Deflación cuántica variacional", "Regresión por muestreo cuántico").

examples.source: Subspace Search VQE (SSVQE) {#subspace-search-vqe-ssvqe}
examples.translation: Búsqueda de subespacio VQE (SSVQE) {#subspace-search-vqe-ssvqe}
examples.suggested: VQE de búsqueda en subespacios (SSVQE) {#subspace-search-vqe-ssvqe}
examples.why: The English modifier order is copied, leaving 'VQE' hanging after 'Búsqueda de subespacio'. In Spanish the head noun (VQE) comes first and the modifier after it, which also makes clear that this is a VQE variant.

examples.source: Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) {#variational-quantum-eigensolver-vqe}
examples.translation: Eigensolver Cuántico Variacional (VQE) {#variational-quantum-eigensolver-vqe}
examples.suggested: Eigensolver cuántico variacional (VQE) {#variational-quantum-eigensolver-vqe}
examples.why: Spanish headings use sentence case. The other algorithm headings in this file already do (entry 71 'Deflación cuántica variacional', entry 116 'Regresión por muestreo cuántico'), so this Title Case heading is inconsistent with them.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The CVaR definition keeps its direction (α=1 is the expected value, α=0 is the minimum, and the average is over the "cola inferior"), and the SWAP-strategy and SAT-mapper explanations are accurate. Core terms are used the same way everywhere: compuertas, hamiltoniano, disparos, pase de transpilación, mapeo inicial. There are two small slips. The usage-estimate note switches to the formal "Su tiempo de ejecución", while the rest of the page uses tú. The max-cut goal uses the indicative "de manera que se maximiza" where a purpose clause needs the subjunctive "se maximice".

examples.source: Your runtime may vary.
examples.translation: Su tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.suggested: Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar.
examples.why: This is a formal (usted) slip on a page that otherwise addresses the reader as tú.

examples.source: such that the number of edges between the two sets is maximized
examples.translation: de manera que se maximiza el número de aristas entre los dos conjuntos
examples.suggested: de manera que se maximice el número de aristas entre los dos conjuntos
examples.why: This clause states a goal, so Spanish needs the subjunctive here. The indicative reads like a grammar mistake.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The trade-off (lower two-qubit depth for the AI transpiler, fewer gates for SABRE), the sign convention in the summary table and the caveats about mirror circuits all come through intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. What a native editor would still fix: the product is written three ways ("Transpiler con IA", "transpilador con IA" in [7]/[12], "transpiler estándar"), and gate appears as both "puertas" ([7]) and "gates" everywhere else. There are also a few stiff renderings: "noise floor" becomes "umbral de ruido" (threshold), "shallower circuit" becomes "más superficial", "two-qubit gate depth" loses "gate", and "10,000" keeps the English thousands separator.

examples.source: How the AI-powered transpiler compares to the default transpiler in terms of two-qubit depth, gate count
examples.translation: Cómo se compara el transpilador con IA con el transpilador predeterminado en términos de profundidad de dos qubits, número de puertas
examples.suggested: Cómo se compara el Transpiler con IA con el transpiler predeterminado en términos de profundidad de dos qubits, número de gates
examples.why: Only this entry and [12] use 'transpilador' and 'puertas'. The rest of the file uses 'Transpiler/transpiler' and 'gates', so the terms are inconsistent within the page.

examples.source: where both methods are pushed close to the noise floor
examples.translation: donde ambos métodos se acercan al umbral de ruido
examples.suggested: donde ambos métodos quedan cerca del nivel de ruido de fondo
examples.why: 'Umbral' means threshold, which is a different idea from noise floor, the level of background noise. The usual Spanish term is 'nivel de ruido de fondo' or 'piso de ruido'.

examples.source: the default transpiler produced both a shallower and smaller circuit
examples.translation: produjo tanto un circuit más superficial como más pequeño
examples.suggested: produjo un circuit menos profundo y más pequeño
examples.why: 'Más superficial' is a literal calque. The natural phrasing for circuit depth is 'menos profundo', which is also what [19] uses.

examples.source: **two-qubit gate depth**, **total gate count**
examples.translation: **profundidad de dos qubits**, **conteo total de gates**
examples.suggested: **profundidad de gates de dos qubits**, **conteo total de gates**
examples.why: The translation drops 'gate', so the metric no longer says it counts layers of two-qubit gates. It is still recognizable from context.

editor_note: Both rewritten link labels are faithful and use the same terms as the rest of the page: [54] "Desacoplamiento dinámico" and [55] "Resiliencia, incluyendo mitigación de errores de medición y extrapolación a ruido cero (ZNE)" match entries [11], [12] and [14].

I only judged entry 3, which is faithful and natural: "Estimación de uso: menos de 30 segundos en un procesador Heron r2" keeps the "under 30 seconds" bound, and the caveat is fully there in the informal tú register ("NOTA: Esto es solo una estimación. Tu tiempo de ejecución puede variar.").

All four rewritten entries (13, 36, 42, 47) are faithful and read naturally: they consistently use "problema de reparto de mercado", render "exactly half the total demand" as "exactamente la mitad de la demanda total", and render the transpile_only option as "solo se transpila a un circuito (y no se resuelve)".

All five rewritten entries keep the English meaning. The gamma rescaling and gamma^2 sampling cost in [15], the timeout note in [86] ("nunca subestima el efecto de un error") and the qubit-6 commutation claim in [110] are accurate, and nothing was invented. There are two wording slips. In [16], "eventualmente se estabiliza" uses the false friend "eventualmente", which in Spanish usually means "possibly" rather than "in the end", so it weakens the claim that the overhead does plateau; "acaba estabilizándose" fixes it. In [131], "fijamos el valor más profundo" copies the English "deepest value"; "el valor máximo" reads naturally in Spanish.

examples.source: the required sampling overhead eventually plateaus when scaling the number of qubits
examples.translation: la sobrecarga de muestreo requerida eventualmente se estabiliza al escalar el número de qubits
examples.suggested: la sobrecarga de muestreo requerida acaba estabilizándose al aumentar el número de qubits
examples.why: 'Eventualmente' is a false friend. In Spanish it usually means 'possibly/occasionally', which weakens the claim that the overhead does plateau (Fig. 2b).

examples.source: we set the deepest value to half the circuit's two-qubit-layer depth
examples.translation: fijamos el valor más profundo en la mitad de la profundidad de capas de dos qubits del circuito
examples.suggested: fijamos el valor máximo en la mitad de la profundidad de capas de dos qubits del circuito
examples.why: 'Valor más profundo' copies 'deepest value'. A native technical writer would say 'valor máximo' ('mayor profundidad' is already used earlier in the same entry).
